acceptance: Capture the real React/CSS at 320×568, 390×844, 768×1024, 1023×900, 1440×900 and 1920×1080. Approval follows captures, not this specification.

At 390×844, the default member list exposes seven readable rows, with all ten records available by ordinary scrolling. Count all visible words, including navigation and truth labels; the first screen must remain below 40 words.

Measure the default member detail and initial scanner separately against the same first-screen limit. No logged-in prose block contains eighteen or more words. Do not shrink text, truncate consequences or conceal errors to meet this.
This surface contains no public sequence. Do not add one to satisfy the separate public word-count target.
Desktop is a 440px roster beside a substantial member composition, not a stretched phone list or a spreadsheet.
Sara belongs to Jasmine’s Morning loop Story campaign. Do not adopt the conflicting Maya example in the request; Maya owns the Counter pour Recreate source.
The baseline reconciles to 10 members, 6 repeat visitors, 1 ready reward, 2 redemption events and 28 counted visits.
Counting Sara’s September 17 visit produces 5 of 5, a ready reward and totals 10, 6, 2, 2. Redeeming it produces 0 of 5 and totals 10, 6, 1, 3.
Jasmine’s unique-member attribution changes from 4 joined, 3 came back, 1 redeemed to 4, 3, 2 only after Sara redeems.
A fresh same-day counting attempt appends one zero-delta event. Replaying the same request key appends nothing. Neither changes Wallet content or recent-customer ordering.
Recognition alone never counts a visit. The second same-day scan followed by its counting action produces the explicit unchanged receipt.
An ordinary Noah visit changes 3 of 5 to 4 of 5. The points fixtures change 82 to 83 and 99 to 100 through a fixed one-point award.
Earned rewards survive navigation. Additional progress accumulated while a reward waits survives redemption of that reward.
No camera permission, fake camera feed, production request, real Wallet save, notification delivery or production session change occurs.
Contacts remain masked outside the search input. No full-contact reveal, export or creator-accessible customer route exists.
The requested individual Send update and Block actions resolve to honest capability boundaries. The approved V3 scope prohibits individual messaging and leaves blocking for later.
Test mouse, touch, keyboard, screen reader, browser Back, 200% text zoom and reduced motion. Check focus restoration after every sheet, confirmation and counter exit.
Verify every visible implementation string against this inventory. Names, numbers, dates, entered search values and masked fixture contacts are data exceptions; additional helper copy is not.
spec.signature_moment: The acquisition thread survives the counter transaction: Sara’s fourth mark becomes a fifth, then a redeemed reward, while Joined from Jasmine stays attached. A standalone loyalty product would not connect that return to its original TapMart campaign.

honest_states: Only the V3 in-memory provider supplies members, events and projections. Reload resets it; route changes do not.
The default member is Sara at 4 of 5, not the designer’s historical 3-of-5 specimen.
Ready rewards are earned instances. Their state is not inferred solely from a displayed fraction.
Ava and June have enrolled without a visit. Ben has a visit without Wallet. Neither condition is treated as incomplete membership.
Same-day attempts use America/Chicago calendar days. A recognition is not a counted visit; an explicit counting attempt is required.
A failed commit retains the member, input and idempotency key. No progress animation, unlock, history event or Wallet receipt appears.
A successful fixture update is not a delivered Wallet update. Unsaved-Wallet members receive no simulated device-update receipt.
The Google-limit scenario updates card content but requests no additional notification. Apple ordinary progress changes remain silent content updates.
Source attribution is preserved from the first known acquisition. Counter activity never reassigns Sara to Counter QR.
No business Contact action, full-contact reveal, customer export, individual Wallet update or working Block mutation is introduced.
An unknown member route and an unknown QR are errors, not empty directories.
A no-program or draft context routes the user toward setup; it does not display ten specimen members.
spec.two_second_read: Find the name. See the remaining visit. Count once. If the reward is ready, redeem it without losing the member or source.
media: No portraits appear in the roster or member detail. In particular, /design-lab/portrait-imani-01.jpg is a creator asset, not a portrait of member Imani.

Program artwork uses only /design-lab/reference-loopday-01.jpg. Record intrinsic dimensions and reviewed crop in the V3 manifest before use. Desktop scanner standby: 592×320 maximum, object-fit cover, initial object-position 50% 50%; preserve the photographed subject. Card strips use the separate crop below. If unavailable, show the plain Media unavailable fallback.

Coded loop mark: 32×32 viewBox; open 270-degree circular path centered at 16,16, radius 10, 2px paper stroke with butt ends. A 6px brick terminal continues the lower-right tangent. No enclosing badge, stamp texture or animation. Render 28px in Apple header and within a 40px circular Google logo field.

Coded app progress: five equal 4px-high horizontal strokes across the available progress width, separated by 8px. Completed strokes are #18231D; remaining strokes have a 1px #58625B outline and paper interior. The current newly earned stroke temporarily receives a 12px #B73E28 terminal after commit. No circles, numbered stamps or unsupported native Wallet progress controls. The numeric sentence provides the accessible value.

Points progress uses one straight 4px track with a mathematically proportional ink fill, not 100 tiny stamps. Its complete numeric balance remains the primary value. A ready instance fills the current requirement; retained next-cycle credits are separate details.

Coded member QR: actual SVG QR, fixed version 2, error correction M, 25×25 data modules with a four-module quiet zone on every side. Encode TMV3:M: followed by the member’s twelve-character opaque fixture code. Render at 165×165 CSS pixels: 33 total modules at 5px each. Black #000000 modules, white #FFFFFF background, no logo, corner rounding, colour tint or overlaid scan line. Snap its origin to whole CSS pixels. The readable LD identifier is a separate 13px caption.
The acquisition QR is never rendered on these member surfaces. View QR navigates to the separate signup-QR route. No membership QR is reused as a signup link.

Coded scanner: 264×264 paper aperture at 390 and desktop; 244×244 at 320. Four 24px corner brackets use 2px ink strokes. The idle center is empty paper with a single 20px regular scan icon; no photograph, noise, video, camera chrome or pulsing laser. The scanner is labelled directly, not through a distant footer.

On recognition, the aperture becomes a member identification area of the same bounds: first name and masked suffix along its top; 165px member QR centered below; readable ID below the QR. The central result has an opaque paper backing. A one-time recognition sweep may remain visible only in the outer 8px gutters, never across the QR or text.

Apple concept: 375px reference width, approximately 520px content-led height, 12px outer radius, solid #18231D, system typography. Header has the loop and Loopday Coffee. A 375:123 strip uses a solid ink left 58% reading area and the Loopday photo in the right 42%; no gradient. Primary VISITS or POINTS sits in the solid area. Below are exactly three combined secondary/auxiliary fields: REWARD, MEMBER and STATUS. QR is 165px on white with LD identifier below. No on-pass button.

Google concept: 375px reference width, approximately 560px content-led height, 12px outer radius and solid #18231D. Circular loop logo, Loopday Rewards, then Loopday Coffee. A 3:1 hero uses the verified Loopday crop with no text overlay. Visits or Points and Rewards balances sit side by side below. Member and Member ID follow, then the 165px QR. Requirement, state, terms and optional offer are in Details, not invented native controls.

Phone native concepts use 358px width at 390 and 296px at 320. Adapt layout rather than scaling all text; keep body values at least 16px and QR at 165px. Wrapper platform labels, No pass is issued., Details and Close remain outside the card.
All shell and action icons reuse the as-built V2 Phosphor regular set: 20px, 1.75px-equivalent optical stroke; navigation 22px. Do not introduce Lucide or another library on this V3 surface.
states: 01, Roster, default: All selected, ten records, compact progress, no contacts, portraits, source paragraphs or engagement scores. On desktop Sara is the initial read-only inspected member; phone remains a list.

02, Roster lookup and filters: query matches normalized first name, phone or email locally. All, Repeat visitors and Reward ready are mutually exclusive status filters; an incoming source filter intersects them. Clear filters removes the source/status restriction. Typing does not change focus or create events.

03, Roster empty/error variants: distinguish no members, no query matches, no ready rewards, no repeat visitors and invalid member URL. A live-zero program offers View QR. No-program and draft contexts show their setup guards.

04, Redemption-event view: view=redemptions shows individual reward-use events, newest first. A member can appear more than once if they have multiple redemption events. This is not labelled as a unique-member total.

05, Member detail, collecting: first name and mask; current progress; five strokes or one points line; reward; primary Add visit or Add points; preserved source thread; Wallet summary; collapsed History. Sara starts at 4 of 5.

06, Member detail, zero/ready/redeemed: zero retains Add visit; ready makes Redeem primary and Add visit secondary; redeemed retains its status until the next counted activity and allows Add visit. A ready instance and additional progress can coexist.

07, Member disclosures: source opens immutable evidence; Wallet opens the current read-only concept; History expands counted and uncounted events. Member actions exposes only the honest Send update and Block boundaries.

08, Recording entry: Scan is default unless the last explicitly used mode was Search. A member query parameter is honored only following an explicit staff action. Opening the counter performs no recording.
09, Scanner idle: labelled empty coded aperture, Sample member selector, Simulate scan and No camera is used. The default sample is Sara.

10, Search mode: aperture and sample selector are replaced by the labelled input and local results. Results contain first name, masked contact and progress. Selecting one enters the same recognition state as scanning.

11, Recognition: member identity and QR are stable; progress and Free coffee precede +1 visit. Points shows 1 point, Per qualifying purchase and Add 1 point. The action is usable immediately, before the recognition animation ends.

12, Ordinary counted result: commit the event and derived state atomically; replace the action with Visit counted. or Point added.; update the final value once. Show Wallet update simulated only for saved-Wallet projections. Done, Next customer and View member remain.

13, Reward unlock: qualifying activity creates an earned instance. The last stroke completes and Reward ready replaces the ordinary caption. Redeem becomes available immediately. It never activates automatically.

14, Same-day result: an explicit fresh counting attempt appends a zero-delta event and shows Already counted today., the unchanged value and the daily rule. No progress movement, reward mutation, Wallet update or recent-list reorder occurs.
15, Unknown QR: reject the sample without displaying a person. Search members changes mode; Try another QR restores the scanner.
16, Recording failure: show the failure in the action region, retain member and request key, and offer Try again. The QA scenario fails the first commit only; the deliberate retry can succeed.
17, Redemption confirmation: bind to one ready earned-instance ID, show the exact reward and no-visit consequence, then Cancel or Redeem reward. Repeated activation of the same request is idempotent.

18, Redemption complete: consume only that instance’s attached credits, append the redemption event and display Reward redeemed. Retain next-cycle progress and any other ready instances. Wallet and source identity remain.
19, Redemption error/stale state: failed mutation leaves the ready instance unchanged. An already-consumed instance returns This reward is no longer ready. rather than creating a second event.
20, Next customer: clear recognized identity, result receipt and request key; return to the selected Scan or Search mode. Clear the search query for privacy. Keep the current demo day.
21, Focused exit: Done or Close returns to the exact originating roster/detail position. Browser Back first closes a confirmation or disclosure, then the counter. Fixture state remains.

22, Lab scenarios: replacement contexts are explicit and confirmed. Advance demo day changes the business calendar day without resetting progress. No hidden clock progression or automatic replay occurs.

accessibility: Use semantic navigation, a search form, a list of member links, real buttons and disclosure controls. Do not build the roster as an ARIA data grid.
Every icon-only Back, Close, Clear search and Member actions control has the exact accessible name in the copy inventory and a minimum 44×44px target.

Use 2px brick focus outlines with 3px offset on light surfaces and paper focus outlines on ink. Selected filters also have aria-pressed; Business has aria-current.
Names and campaign names may wrap. Requirements, reward states, errors and action consequences never truncate.
Search-result updates are announced politely as a numeric result count without moving focus. Do not announce every keystroke or expose full matching contacts.
On scan recognition, move focus to the member summary and make the counting action immediately next in reading order. After commit, announce one complete result, not each changed field.
Redemption confirmation traps focus and starts on its heading. Cancel returns to Redeem; completion returns to the result’s Done control.
Browser Back and Escape close the top disclosure or confirmation first. Returning from the counter restores the exact originating link and scroll anchor.
Keep forms usable with the software keyboard open. No fixed counter action can cover search results or error text.
At 200% text zoom, permit reflow and longer page height. At effective phone widths, drop desktop companions and preserve all material copy.
Member routes remain business-only in the isolated route model. Personal and creator previews expose no member identity, QR, contact or individual event timestamp.

motion.explains: One earned instance was consumed, not the member or unrelated progress.

motion.name: Redeem and keep the thread

motion.explains: A no-op or failure is not a successful progress event.

motion.name: No false progress
motion.what_moves: Nothing moves. An explicit text result appears in the reserved action/receipt region.

on_demand: Roster query begins when the input receives focus. Match trimmed, case-folded names, normalized phone digits and lowercased email. Results never expose the matched full contact.

Selecting a roster member opens /design-lab-v3/business/loyalty/members/:memberId. Desktop replaces the inspected region; phone and tablet open the full detail. Preserve list query, filters and scroll.
Incoming filter=repeat|ready|redeemed and source=<fixture-source-id> remain views of the same cohort. view=redemptions switches to events; do not silently interpret an event total as unique people.

Tapping the source thread opens Source details: human source, campaign, named acquisition link or QR, Joined timestamp, recorded first-touch evidence when available and the two short preservation explanations. It does not expose a creator profile with customer data.

Tapping History expands the latest counted visit, lifetime count and chronological event list. Each event starts with its concise label and date; tapping an event exposes its actual time. Same-day attempts remain visibly zero-delta history.
Tapping Free coffee or the progress summary opens reward details and the applicable version’s terms. Retained progress and ready-instance quantity appear here when relevant.

View demo card opens /design-lab-v3/card/:memberCode with the member’s saved platform selected. Show demo card opens the same read-only wrapper without changing Wallet state. This surface has no Add to Wallet action.

The card wrapper’s Details reveals Reward, Requirement, Terms, Member ID and Offer only if present. It never reveals phone or email. Platform switching changes representation, not saved-platform state.

Tapping Member actions opens Send update and Block. Send update opens the program-wide boundary, then optionally View Wallet updates at /design-lab-v3/business/loyalty/updates with no member recipient parameter. Block opens its unavailable explanation and changes nothing.
Add visit or Add points from a detail opens /design-lab-v3/business/loyalty/record?member=<fixture-id>. Global roster Add visit or Scan opens unselected Scan mode.
Simulate scan resolves Sample member immediately. Unknown QR and Other-program QR produce the same boundary error, never a guessed identity.
View member from recording preserves the counter session and opens the recognized member detail. Browser Back returns to that result rather than counting again.
Details on a same-day receipt reveals the actual last-counted time. Details on a Wallet receipt reveals Nothing was sent.; the Google-cap case adds its two explicit allowance statements.
Redeem opens only the compact earned-instance confirmation. There is no celebratory modal and no automatic reward consumption.

The Design Lab context opens the scenario selector, Reset demo and Demo time. Scenario changes and resets require confirmation. Advance demo day increments the America/Chicago calendar date while retaining 10:00 AM and existing events.
Inherited unimplemented shell actions open Outside this preview. They never reach production or fabricate business messaging, settings or campaign states.
